desc:
The array bits contains only 0 and 1. In one swap you may exchange the values at any two positions (they need not be neighbours). Return the minimum number of swaps needed so that all the 1s end up in one contiguous block. If there are no 1s, the answer is 0.

bits = [1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1]
four 1s, so look at windows of length 4: none contains more than two 1s, e.g. [1,0,1,0]
result = 4 - 2 = 2
hints: In the final arrangement the 1s occupy a block whose length equals the total number of 1s, call it m.
Pick the block position first. Each 0 currently inside that block needs one swap with a 1 from outside it.
So the cost of a block is m minus the number of 1s already inside it. Find the window of length m with the most 1s.
editorial: Let m be the number of ones. Wherever the final block of length m goes, the zeros currently inside it must be exchanged with ones currently outside, and each swap fixes exactly one zero (there are always as many outside ones as inside zeros). The cost is therefore the count of zeros in the block.

Minimizing zeros in a length-m window is the same as maximizing ones in it. A fixed-size sliding window with a running count of ones does this in O(n) time and O(1) space. The answer is m - maxOnes, and 0 when m is 0.
